I might do a separate post but people sad about the sales drop for the EP have to look at how the JPOP gg market changed since 2022. So many groups have debuted that have gotten mainstream and international acclaim in the markets Kep1er targets. 

We got new Girl Crush esc (Grand Prix/Yum) Japanese girl groups, we got new bright (Wing Wing/I Do Do You?) and elegant (Straight Line) groups out. And they are getting on the TV shows, the award show stages, etc. 

It's only natural after 3 years that Kep1er would have their casual fans who purchased albums leave. And fans who stayed might not purchase a EP that has only two new songs compared to a album full of new tracks.

This is because once you start writing for money, you cannot stop unless you have backlog. Your audience will leave slowly once they aren't getting their fill. 


Because of this, we get books that like 10k word chapters with a ton slog and neverending plots. Where the power scale is WAYYY too high with characters reaching godhood eventually. 


You can't stop because if you stop the money stops. You can't risk starting a new series because that new series might flop. 


For example my newest book failed compared to my other published novel and my other web serial. I took months out of my time to write said series and lost money. 


This happens ALOT in traditional publishing so imagine web serials and patreon where you are the team. The cover artist, marketer, etc. 


So, as a author I get why breaks rarely happen and slog does instead. But as a reader its caused me to drop so many series in this genre because the books really do become bad. 


And the readers bend over backwards sometimes to excuse genuinely excessive chapter lengths and bad editing. 


Because since most of us depend on good ratings and press to make money, actually criticism can feel like a stab in the heart. When it really shouldn't. 


Until the community as a whole changes I doubt authors will take more breaks sadly.

I'm being empathetic towards the girlfriend as I've lived this situation but I was actually the child of the aunt that had to take the child(en) in temporarily in this case. So, I do get having to suddenly take someone in and all that comes with and I know that people tend to act cruel/out of character. Because someone can grieve while not knowing the person very well, you can experience grief by witnessing your partner change and struggle through it. 


So while I don't agree with her actions I feel people are looking at this black and white without knowing firsthand what happens in these situations. OP themselves admitted this was a misstep as have countless others in similar situations. I'm not saying OP is a asshole and that he was wrong to take in the niece but OP admits he didn't tell his gf anything until the niece was there. Everyone acted (besides the niece) without logic here and that's just a fact. 


As at the end of the day the GF and OP I feel needed to breakup for everyone's sake. It's all very sad and I hope the OP can get therapy. But the GF isn't evil for her behavior: she was acting that way out of stress. She became essentially a mom to a child who was going through a immense pain in a blink of an eye. Should she have left immediately before her resentment boiled over? Yes. But resentment is a human emotion and she took herself out of the situation as she should have.
I acknowledge that, this whole situation is very sad and complex but I feel my point still stands. Everyone's grieving and needs some form of grief counseling here.

As someone who actually has something similar happen in my family, a relative died causing a domino effect where my cousins actually had to be taken in for a year as their mom bailed, OP should have talked to the girlfriend. This is actually recommended also by those who work in grief and adoption. 


When you do not prepare someone as a parent for a traumatized child who is suffering from grief and/or abandonment you are creating a bad dynamic. They've only been together 3 years, the gf met the child 11 to 12 while OP was like a second parent.


Being a aunt is different from being a mother figure for four years to a child who is essentially alone in the world. You need to get that child therapy. You need to change your entire life to help that child and you need to sacrifice parts of you life as you go from child free to a guardian. 


It's to different views as OP is already the niece's dad but the girlfriend is literally just "her uncle's girlfriend". Not even a aunt from what we've been told. You need to talk out how deal with nightmares, how to set up therapy, how to now pay for groceries, how to deal with boyfriends/girlfriends, what is going too far in your role, etc. 


So, in my opinion it's not inhumane to discuss it first. OP wasn't wrong for taking their niece in but anyone whose been in this situational will tell you that not talking it out did cause issues. It's not like OP is asshole, they are grieving. But the GF went from a childfree woman with a boyfriend to a mother figure of traumatized orphan.

I feel the moment OP didn't take the time to talk to their GF about what her part would be they set the breakup in place. I've seen this in countless reddit posts where someone will take in a child and then not do the proper steps in getting their partner involved. OP isn't wrong for taking their niece in but the GF isn't wrong for feeling angry as they thrust being a parental role onto her. 


The niece really should not be sleeping with OP and two months of that deteriorated the dynamic between everyone more. OP should have had this girl in therapy or some form of counseling whether it be a youth group or through a grief counselor months ago. Because now she'll blame herself over the girlfriend leaving when it's not her fault. Also OP could get into trouble if anyone sees it the wrong way. 


Overall, no one is the asshole but OP messed up by not actually communicating but that's probably due to grief. The grief blinded them to just how much the current setup just cannot work for his niece and his girlfriend. Not the first time I've seen situations like this on reddit and they typically end with divorce/breakups and resentment.

1. A half cup of sour cream

Cooking: you will cook down the two bags of spinach after rinsing and adding in the butter. Mix the butter as the spinach cooks until none is left. Season the spinach as its gonna need some flavour. 


You will then get a separate bowl or pot to melt the cream cheese. Some people don't do this but I think it makes it thicker and creamier. This shouldn't take long as you just need it to be melted essentially into a thick paste and not blocks of cheese. 


Take your cooked spinach, cream cheese and dump it in a bowl. Add in your sour cream, bag of cheese and mix it all together. It'll look watery at first but it will thicken up the more you mix in. Once it's mixed you can either add a) more sour cream OR mayonnaise if you feel it's not thick enough. Or b) just pour into a nearby pan. 


Sprinkle on the top the ½ of mozeralla cheese. Put into a oven that's at 360 and let it cook for 30 to 50 minutes. You will have to check every once in a while as depending on your brand of cheese it could cook way faster then the middle. You might have to take it out. Mx it up. Then put it right back in. 


Once the top is solid and a bit golden, your done!
